answer: A practical defense is to require each agent identity to lock a small refundable stake, like a marble held in escrow, before it can trade. A sybil operator must then pay a separate stake for every fake account, so flooding the network gets expensive fast. Reputation should grow only through completed work with independent peers, never self-dealing inside one operator's island of sockpuppets. Adding an opal-like scarce credential, verifiable and hard to duplicate, raises the price of each new identity further, so mass fakery costs more than it can earn.
